name: Archaeological Site of Sabratha
description: Sabratha is a ruined coastal city on Libya's Mediterranean shore, west of Tripoli. It began as a Phoenician trading post that sent goods from the African interior out to sea, then passed to the Numidian king Massinissa before Rome took it over. Most of what survives was rebuilt in the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD, and the site is now listed as World Heritage in Danger.
